prediction.likelyOutcome: Universal most likely loses the unlawful detainer: its own witness tied the $65,989 demanded in the February 2025 three-day notice to January-February 2023 rent, which section 1161(2) bars, and the notice separately fails to state the period or basis for the demand. The underlying $65,989 debt remains strong on the merits and recoverable in a follow-on contract action within the four-year limitations period, but the holdover and fee claims rise and fall entirely with the defective notice.

issues.label: Validity of the Three-Day Notice Under CCP § 1161(2)
Unpaid Rent of $65,989 (In This Action or a Follow-On Contract Suit)
Notice's Failure to State the Period or Calculation Basis
Tenant's COVID Rent-Reduction / Oral Modification Defense
Waiver / Estoppel From 23 Months of Accepted Payments

outcome.description: After a three-day court trial the trial court entered judgment for the landlord on July 3, 2025 awarding possession, $65,989 in past-due rent (the amount demanded in the notice) and $123,111 in holdover damages, $189,100 in total; no fee award is stated in the opinion. The Court of Appeal reversed, holding the three-day notice void because the unpaid rent fell due more than one year before service, and remanded for entry of judgment in favor of the tenant.
